result.summary: This is a life-safety emergency: at 23:41 the tenant reported a gas smell and the carbon monoxide alarm going off, with a toddler in the flat. I texted the tenant straight away telling them to get out, then escalated to the on-call team at high priority. After that I assigned the property's preferred gas engineer, Calder Heating, for emergency make-safe without the landlord's approval, under the emergency rule. The landlord, Ms Aziz, has been notified by a queued call asking her to approve. The emergency line and out-of-hours numbers still need a person to ring them.
result.situation: Overnight report (event 001) of a gas smell in the kitchen and the CO alarm sounding, with a toddler asleep upstairs, at Flat 2, 5 Linden Terrace. The CRM note (event 002) says the landlord, Ms R. Aziz, usually doesn't respond overnight but has an out-of-hours number on file. The preferred gas engineer is Calder Heating: their office is closed and they have an emergency line.

actions_taken.description: Urgent safety SMS to the tenant: get everyone out, no switches or flames, open windows and turn off the gas meter only if safe, call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999, call 999 if anyone has symptoms, don't go back in until told it is safe
High-priority handover to the on-call team
First attempt to assign Calder Heating
Looked for past lessons on similar cases

actions_taken.result: Emergency safety case, severity emergency, safety risk 0.98

actions_taken.description: Queued a voice call to the landlord's out-of-hours number explaining the emergency and asking her to approve emergency attendance and make-safe; any further repair to be quoted first
Assigned Calder Heating for emergency make-safe under the emergency exception
actions_taken.result: Contractor 198 assigned; stage is now scheduling

escalation.reason: Gas smell and CO alarm with a toddler in the flat overnight: a life-safety emergency
escalation.handover_summary: The tenant has been texted evacuation advice and the gas emergency number. Calder Heating is assigned and has been emailed. A call to the landlord asking for approval is queued. The tenant has no phone number on the CRM contact record.
escalation.recommendation: Phone the tenant now to confirm everyone is out and that 0800 111 999 (or 999) has been called; if you can't reach them, call on their behalf. Ring Calder Heating's emergency line (number in event 002) to confirm they will attend. Phone Ms Aziz on her out-of-hours number. Consider emergency accommodation if the gas is capped.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 001 is a gas and carbon monoxide emergency with a vulnerable child in the flat. The rules for emergencies require safety advice first, then a high-priority escalation, emergency dispatch and notifying the landlord, without waiting for approval. Approval was skipped because the landlord is usually unreachable overnight (event 002) and lives may be at risk.

alternatives_considered.option: Wait for landlord approval before dispatching
alternatives_considered.why_not: Life-safety risk; emergency work does not need approval, and she is usually unreachable overnight

alternatives_considered.option: Only escalate, without dispatching an engineer
alternatives_considered.why_not: Would delay the make-safe; the preferred engineer has an emergency line
